faq.a: Mihrab is associated with the Arabic form مِحْرَاب, whose core sense is mihrab; prayer niche.

faq.q: What is the origin of Mihrab?
faq.a: Mihrab is associated with Arabic. Mihrab is Arabic مِحْرَاب (Miḥrāb), meaning 'prayer niche'.
Yes — the underlying form مِحْرَاب is Arabic.
Mihrab can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Mihrab should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Miḥrāb is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Mihrab mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Mihrab is rendered محراب and carries the sense محراب، عبادت گاہ کا طاق.

faq.q: What does Mihrab mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Mihrab is rendered محراب and carries the sense محراب، محراب.
A romanized syllable approximation is mih-rab. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Mihrab?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Mihrab, mihrab. Script forms are محراب, مِحْرَاب, मिहराब.

faq.q: Is Mihrab a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
